turns.text:
My husband canceled our next couples therapy session without telling me first. I found out from the confirmation email. He says he can't sit in there not knowing who's going to hear about it, because I talked to my sister.

In August, in a session, he said he's not sure he wants kids anymore. We were supposed to start the adoption process in the spring. I cried in that room. On the drive home I asked if we could talk about it and he said, "Not tonight." After each of our first three sessions I'd asked the same thing, and every time he said he'd said what he needed to in the room. Kavya is who I talk to most days. Of course I talked to her.

Saturday, at my nephew's birthday, she said something to him about it. She shouldn't have. He texted me "I'm going home" and left in our car, so I was stranded at my sister's until 6. He's told a friend from work we're in therapy, but my sister is off limits? I feel so alone in this. I think he's been looking for a way out of therapy since August, and this handed him one.

How do I raise this with him without it turning into a fight?

That sounds lonely. In August you heard in that room that he might not want kids anymore, with adoption planned for spring. You cried, then asked on the drive home to talk and heard "not tonight." He'd already said three times that he'd said what he needed to in the room. Then you learned from a confirmation email that he'd canceled the next session, and on Saturday you were left at your sister's until 6 after he took the car. Of course you feel alone in this.

Some of that is fair to be upset about however the rest turns out. Canceling a joint session without telling you first, so you found out from an email, is a reasonable thing to raise. So is leaving with the only car and a one-line text.

Other parts I can't settle from here, because I haven't heard him. You two may see differently what was okay to share with Kavya, or whether you ever had an understanding about it. Him telling a work friend you're in therapy may feel different to him than your sister knowing what was said in a session and bringing it up at a family party. You've both agreed she shouldn't have said anything to him. Whether he's been looking for a way out since August is your guess at what's going on inside him. It might be part of it, or it might not. What his actions clearly show is that he doesn't feel safe in that room right now. They don't show why.

To keep this from turning into a fight, you could start with the thing you both already agree on, and then ask instead of argue. Something like:

*"I know Kavya shouldn't have said anything to you on Saturday, and I'm sorry you got put on the spot. I talked to her because after August I didn't have anywhere else to take it. You'd said you'd said what you needed to in the room. I want to understand what would make therapy feel safe enough for you to go back. Can you tell me?"*

That opens with what you both agree on and explains your side without accusing him. It also leaves him room to tell you what he needs. The cancellation and the car can come next, once he's not bracing to defend himself.

Whether to say that, and when, is up to you. If you'd like, we can work on how to raise the cancellation and Saturday too.

You're right to feel hurt and alone. You're right that finding out about the cancellation from an email, and being left at your sister's without a car, are fair things to be upset about. And you're right that after August you needed someone to talk to and weren't getting that from him.

Whether you were right to tell Kavya what was said in session, or whether he's right that it broke something, I can't say. That depends on things only the two of you know: what you'd each assumed about privacy, and what it felt like for him to hear it from her at a party. Same with why he canceled. Your guess might be part of it, but I've only heard your side, and he'd likely tell it differently.

I know that's not the yes you were hoping for. But you don't need to win the question of who's right to have a real conversation with him. You can go in knowing your hurt is legitimate and still be curious about his.
